title: Can you finish the courses?
statement:
A training program has `n` courses numbered 0 to n - 1. Each pair `[a, b]` in `prereqs` means you must finish course b before course a.

Return true if it is possible to finish every course.

examples.explanation: Each course waits on the other.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can a course be its own prerequisite?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: It can appear in the input; that makes finishing impossible.
clarifyingQuestions.why: A self-loop is the smallest cycle.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can the same pair appear twice?
Do I need the order, or just whether it’s possible?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Either cycle detection or topological sort works.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How many courses and prerequisites?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Linear in courses plus edges is expected.

edgeCases.input: A cycle among some courses only
edgeCases.why: Still false even if other courses are fine.

edgeCases.input: A diamond (two paths to the same course)

approaches.name: DFS cycle detection
approaches.idea: Color nodes white, gray (on the current path) and black (done). Reaching a gray node means a cycle.
approaches.tradeoffs: Concise, but recursion depth can reach V.

approaches.name: Kahn’s algorithm (topological sort)
approaches.idea: Count prerequisites per course. Repeatedly take courses with zero remaining prerequisites, lowering the counts of courses that depend on them. If every course gets taken, there is no cycle.
approaches.tradeoffs: Iterative and also produces a valid order.

optimal.name: Kahn’s algorithm
optimal.explanation: Build an adjacency list from each prerequisite to the courses it unlocks and an in-degree count. Start with all zero in-degree courses. Pop one, count it done, and decrement its dependents, adding any that reach zero. Return done == n.

hintLadder: Model courses as a graph. What does an edge mean?
When is it impossible to finish?
Which courses can you take right away?
Repeatedly take courses with no remaining prerequisites (topological sort); if some never become available, there is a cycle.

followUps: Return one valid order to take the courses.

walkthrough.say: So b then a for each pair. Could a course list itself as a prerequisite? And I only need to say whether it’s possible, not the order?
Courses are nodes and each pair is an edge from b to a. Finishing everything is possible exactly when there’s no cycle.

I’ll use a topological sort. Count how many prerequisites each course is waiting on. Start with the courses waiting on nothing; finishing one lowers the count for courses after it. If I can finish all n, there was no cycle, because a cycle’s courses would wait on each other forever. That’s O(V plus E).
Build the edges and waiting counts.
Take ready courses and unlock their dependents.
For 3 courses with 0 then 1 then 2: only 0 is ready; finishing it readies 1, then 2. Done is 3, true.
For the two-course cycle, both are waiting on one course, so nothing is ready, done is 0, false. A self-loop is the same: the course waits on itself.
O(V plus E) time and space. If they wanted the order, I’d record courses as I pop them.
